evidence.source: shuowen_jiezi
evidence.text: 不宜有也。《春秋傳》曰：“日月有食之。”从月又聲。凡有之屬皆从有。

evidence.source: wiktionary
evidence.text:
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ɢʷɯʔ): phonetic 又 (OC *ɢʷɯs) + semantic 肉 (“meat”). The hand shape has been abstracted to 𠂇; compare 右, where 又 has also taken this shape. The 肉 in turn has taken the form of ⺼.
The character may have been the original form of 侑 (OC *ɢʷɯs, “to urge to eat”). Alternatively, it may be the original form of 醢 (OC *qʰɯːʔ, “minced pickled meat”), which also has the 又 (OC *ɢʷɯs) element as phonetic.
Folk etymology traditionally explains it as a hand holding meat, hence “in possession of”. However, the oracle bone script shows no meat.
Shuowen Jiezi and other ancient sources have erroneously analyzed the character as a phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ɢʷɯʔ): phonetic 又 (OC *ɢʷɯs) + semantic 月 (“moon”). Shuowen Jiezi defines 有 as "不宜有也" ("[to have something that] not should be had"), citing the Spring and Autumn Annals (春秋傳): "日月有食之" ("There are solar and lunar eclipses"). As eclipses were not auspicious to the Chinese, they were "something that should not be happening". The 月 component alludes to the inauspicious lunar eclipse.
Possibly Sino-Tibetan. Compare Tibetan ཡོད (yod, “to be; to have”). Related to:
* 侑 (OC *ɢʷɯs, “to offer, to sacrifice”) [causative, i.e. “to cause to have”]
* 又 (OC *ɢʷɯs, “again”) [adverbial]
* 或 (OC *ɡʷɯːɡ, “some; or”) [indefinite]

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 有 entry
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes the transmitted 說文 analysis (从月，又聲) from a modern graphic account: bronze forms are analyzed as 又 (hand) plus 肉, depicting a hand holding meat; it calls the 月 account a misreading. It cites the bronze inscription 叔尸鐘「咸有九州」 for possession and notes 有𤔲 as a title corresponding to later 有司. This supports a competing graphic account, but does not by itself establish that the hand-and-meat scene is the earliest meaning.
evidence.title: 有 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 甲骨文 semantic-use discussion, citing 楊逢彬 2003 and 張玉金 2001
evidence.text: A 2024 linguistics article reports that oracle-bone examples of 有 are used for existence, not possession, citing 有虎? 亡其鹿? (《合集》893正); it says the traditional hand-holding-meat interpretation is possible as possession or as existence, since possession presupposes existence. This is a scholarly semantic analysis, not a direct independent inspection of the cited inscription image.
evidence.title: 外

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 有 entry, source-dependent graphic accounts and dated/classical examples
evidence.text: Its account says bronze 有 is 又 plus 肉, while also noting that bronze 又 and 㞢 can be read as 有. It gives 叔尸鐘「咸有九州」 for possession and 有𤔲 as an official title. Its page lists 141 bronze examples but shows the archaeological date/context of the specific quoted vessel only by its bibliographic record, not in the retrieved text; an exact inscription date was therefore not asserted here.
evidence.title: 有 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: CUHK article in 外
evidence.text: The article reports the oracle-bone example 有虎? 亡其鹿? (《合集》893正) as existential. It gives 有大雨? / 無雨? as contrasting existence examples and cites the received text 《老子》「有無相生」 and 《玉篇》 (梁代, 543 CE) glosses 有、不無 and 無、不有. Its argument is that existence is the earliest recoverable sense and possession developed from it; the earliest examples support use, but do not alone date the later semantic extension.
evidence.title: 外

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The entry describes oracle-bone and bronze 又 as a side view of a right hand, with right-hand meaning; it says the graph was later borrowed for ‘again/further’ and 右 came to represent right/rightness. It also reports oracle-bone 又 used for 有 (example 又(有)大雨), and bronze use for assistance (天亡又(佑)王). The account distinguishes whole-graph borrowing for 又 ‘again’ from 又 as a component in 有.
evidence.title: 又 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 說文解字 online transcription with 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The transmitted 說文 says 「不宜有也」, quotes 「日月有食之」, and analyzes 有 as 从月又聲. 段玉裁 interprets the gloss as ‘what should not occur but occurs’, says it extended to the general sense of 有, and explains the 月 association through eclipses; his note on 又聲 gives 云九切 and says 有 was often borrowed for 又 in ancient texts. This is evidence for the historical account, not confirmation of the early graph's components.
evidence.title: 說文解字「有」

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The Sinica Small School Hall oracle database was identified as an authoritative glyph corpus, but its interactive character-level record was not retrieved; the discussion of early forms relies on CUHK's textual analysis and the scholarly article's reported examples rather than visual inspection of primary glyph images.

The earliest 有 attestation's exact inscriptional date, all contextual readings, and whether individual oracle forms visibly contain a meat component remain unverified here. The scholarly article reports a Heji example but is not a primary facsimile.

The CUHK dictionary calls 有 from hand plus meat in bronze forms, whereas modern popular accounts and the scholarly article discuss hand/meat interpretations for earlier forms. Exact graphic chronology and whether meat is present in all early variants remain unresolved; do not describe the transmitted components 月 + 又 as the original graphic structure.

The semantic direction from early existence to possession is argued by the cited 2024 article, but remains a scholarly interpretation; the sparse cited examples do not establish a dated, stepwise path for every extension.

No independently recoverable name or pronunciation of a depicted meat/object is relevantly established. No phonetic-loan derivation from an object name was verified; 又 is treated as a proposed sound component, not as a whole-graph borrowing claim.

The specific Unicode Unihan page for U+6709 was attempted twice and inaccessible. Local exact row is available in sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt but cannot be cited as externally inspected official page content.

The exact local Baxter–Sagart rows show 有 *[ɢ]ʷəʔ and 又 *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s; these differ in notation from Zhengzhang *ɢʷɯʔ in the packet. The Oxford page verifies the 2014 reconstruction's bibliographic identity, but the tool did not expose its exact character rows for independent external validation.
No primary evidence in the inspected sources substantiates the suggested relation of 有 as an original graph for 侑 or 醢; those alternatives remain unverified.
No individual primary oracle-bone facsimile or Sinica record for 有 was opened; the exact earliest attestation, context, and whether particular early variants visibly include meat remain unresolved.

The CUHK source provides a bronze-form 又 + 肉 analysis and quotes a possession use, but the retrieved page does not establish that this is the earliest meaning or provide a precise date for the quoted vessel. The proposed semantic path from existence to possession remains an interpretation rather than a securely dated sequence.

The transmitted 說文 analysis 月 + 又聲 is documented as historical analysis; CUHK rejects 月 as a misreading for its bronze examples. No direct glyph-image comparison was made here to adjudicate every early variant or possible graphic corruption.

No external exact Unihan character page was retrievable for 有 or 又. Local current readings are identified as local evidence only. The exact B–S character rows likewise come from local supplied data, while the linked publisher page confirms only the reconstruction work's bibliographic scope.
The article on early existential use and the reported 合集 893 example were not reopened in this invocation, so they are not counted as new external verification.

No exact Commons file description and direct image URL for 有 oracle or bronze forms was verified. The only selected image candidate is a modern digital seal-style reconstruction, not an artifact photograph.

No independently supported whole-graph borrowing derivation from the name of a depicted object was found. The CUHK discussion supports 又 as a hand-shaped graph and reports its use for 有; it does not establish a recoverable name or pronunciation for a depicted object.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; digital file uploaded 2006, revised 2007
items.tradition: Seal-script style reconstruction based on the Shuowen tradition
items.caption: A seal-script-style form of 有 presents the received Shuowen tradition’s graphic shape. The transmitted Shuowen account analyzes it as 月 with 又 as the sound element, while a modern account of bronze forms instead identifies 又 and 肉; this reconstruction does not establish the character’s earliest structure.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style graph 有, with three horizontal strokes above a rounded central form and a long descending stroke on the right, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: It is a clearly identified illustration of the received seal-style form and helps distinguish that tradition from the competing analysis of bronze forms. It is a modern reconstruction, not an ancient artifact image.
items.rights: Public domain dedication for the SVG representation, as stated on the file description page.

limitations.text: No verifiable image of an oracle-bone or bronze form is included, so the competing early graphic analyses cannot be compared directly here. The bronze account identifies 又 plus 肉, but whether that structure applies to particular early forms and what the earliest structure was remain unresolved.
